text:
maria.k: quick sync — want to follow up on the hierarchical quota shim idea i sketched in the RFC. goal: allow safe per-tenant bursts but cap worst-case shard impact with a thin safety bound + abuse feedback loop.

jake: curious about the enforcement point — edge proxy or admission service?

maria.k: edge for fast fail (cheap CPU), admission for authoritative accounting. idea is two-layer: edge soft-cap, admission hard-cap.

priya: can you outline the tradeoffs? sounds like duplication of logic.

maria.k: yes duplication but reduces tail latency for well-behaved traffic. edge soft-cap = quick 429/soft-shed. admission hard-cap = final source-of-truth and telemetry.

samir: what about consistency across regions? if edge soft-caps in us-east but admission in eu-west, tenants might see weird failures.

maria.k: admission is global-ish. edges take local signals + recent fail history from admission (small bloom / token). sync window intentionally loose (1-2s) — conservative by design.

jake: how do we avoid gameability? clients could spread requests to many edges.

maria.k: second part of proposal: abuse-feedback loop. admission detects anomalous patterns (high 429 ratio, tiny success latencies, repeated short bursts) and emits an "abuse score" that edges can consume. high score => edges lower soft-cap aggressively.

priya: scoring heuristic examples?

maria.k: initial heuristics: 429/sec per tenant, 95th p99 vs p50 latency delta, retry fingerprinting (same client id + short backoff), entropy of prompt sizes. we want simple signals to start.

samir: sounds heavy on telemetry. cost?

maria.k: minimal to start — counters and small histograms per tenant aggregated at admission. storage TTL short (1h) and rollups for long-term.

jake: what's the shim interface between edge & admission? defined proto?

maria.k: sketch: Edge -> Admission check: { tenant_id, token_bucket_hint, recent_local_burst, sequence_id } Admission -> Edge response: { allowed_tokens, safety_bound, abuse_score, decision_id }. Edge uses safety_bound and abuse_score to modulate soft-cap.

priya: can we keep payload tiny? under 256 bytes ideally.

maria.k: yes — only a few ints + short abuse_score (0-100) and a small opaque decision_id string.

samir: rollout plan? risky to flip on global.

maria.k: propose staged rollout: 1) shadow mode at edge + admission: edges send checks but ignore response; admission records and computes abuse_score. 2) soft-enforce for small percent of tenants (canary customers) 3) broader enforcement with auto-fallback.

jake: auto-fallback meaning if admission cloud is unreachable edge falls back to local leaky-bucket?

maria.k: exactly. edge maintains local window when admission unavailable. how much risk? small.

priya: what about fairness across tenants? how do we ensure weighted fairness vs simple caps?

maria.k: safety_bound is per-shard and per-tenant. admission computes: allowed = min(global_alloc*weight, tenant_commit+burst_quota, shard_safety). weights come from billing + SLA. We keep fairness logic in admission only.

samir: do we need to change token accounting model? token-bank vs reservoir?

maria.k: not immediately. admission will present a thin view: allowed_tokens. token-bank remains source-of-truth for long-term quotas. admission consults token-bank for committed budget, but safety_bound prevents single-shard exhaustion.

jake: telemetry / SLOs we should track?

maria.k: short list: 1) edge soft-deny rate by tenant 2) admission hard-deny rate 3) abuse_score distribution 4) cross-region mismatch rate 5) misclassified benign workload rate (false positives)

priya: false positives are dangerous for PLG users. need rapid rollback path per-tenant.

maria.k: rollback via decision_id: admit publishes decisions; operator can revoke decision_id => edges will ignore for that tenant for 10m. Also default is conservative — require 3 signals before high abuse score.

samir: any perf numbers? additional p99 latency at edge?

maria.k: edge check adds ~300-600us for a local in-memory check when cached; remote admission call adds ~2.5ms median, p99 ~8ms with current infra. cache paths avoid calls most of the time.

jake: can we batch admission calls on the edge for hot tenants?

maria.k: yes batching already in the plan — group check for tenant every 50ms. tradeoff: slightly coarser control but much lower RPC QPS.

priya: security implications? decision_id opaque helps audit. need to ensure abuse-score can't be spoofed by tenant.

maria.k: admission signs decision_id with service key; edges verify signature. abuse-score only trusted from admission.

jake: how to test? simulation harness?

maria.k: plan: run replay tests with historical traffic on canary admission to see false positive rates, run synthetic abuse (burst + retries) to validate mitigation, and A/B some real tenants.

samir: any impact on Dedicated / Private deployments?

maria.k: for Dedicated we offer a local admission binary (same logic) with config for safety bounds. For Private on-prem, shipping admission component is optional; if absent, edges operate with local policies only and no global abuse signal. document that in the deployment guide.

priya: do we need infra changes to token-bank?

maria.k: small read API to return tenant committed budget + short-lived reserve hints. low risk.

maria.k: next steps: I can write the follow-up RFC with proto sketch, rollout checklist, and telemetry dashboard queries. anyone volunteer to review?

jake: happy to review the proto and security bits.

samir: I'll help with simulation harness and rollout playbook.

priya: I'll try to write the dashboard queries and FP detection metrics.

maria.k: thanks — i'll draft RFC by EOD tomorrow and @deploy-bot will post a link when ready. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: RFC draft published: https://redwood.internal/rfcs/1725556789-hierarchical-quota-shim (permissions: eng-infra, eng-platform)

priya: got it, reading now.

jake: reading — will comment inline."
